- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33), model underestimates; adjust downward bias by adding 10–20% to forecast.
- Model often overshoots after sharp spikes in sentiment (e.g., 1.00 followed by 1.00), especially in 30d horizon; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast 2–3 days after spike.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d forecasts when sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67); model tends to hold high values; cap forecasts at 1.5–2x recent 7-day average.
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment history shows repeated 1.00/0.33 alternation, model overreacts; apply “sentiment dampening” — reduce forecast by 10–20% if sentiment is oscillating.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after model spike, sentiment was likely negative; adjust forecast downward by 20–40% if sentiment turns negative within 3 days.
